question: Do `--fail-on` and `--max-per-rule` do on a stream of the AC-3 family what they do on a TrueHD stream, and does taking them change anything for a run that gives neither?
method: The checks of the family have been rules since the change before this one, and the two options were still refused there. `verify` takes them now. At `error`, the threshold it has when it is given none, the verdict is read from the counters as it always was; at any other threshold it is the worst finding against the threshold. The limit of the listing reaches the tally the pass files its findings in. A script outside the repository ran `verify --json` with the release binary at every threshold over the three kept streams of the family and the fixture, and with every limit over the fixture with the CRC word of five frames changed. The stream whose only finding is a warning was found by changing each bit of the first frame of the fixture in turn, putting the CRC right and asking `verify`. `tools/old_new.py --decode-all` compared the binary of main before the change with the change, neither run given an option.

reading: They do. A stream whose only finding is a warning exits 0 with no threshold given and 7 at `warning`; a stream with errors exits 7 with none given and 0 at `fatal`; with none given and at `error` every stream is judged alike; and no threshold or limit moves a count. Five findings of a rule are five whatever is listed of them. For a run that gives neither option nothing moves: over 125 streams the same 8 290 lines and 52 448 fields of reports and the same 103 362 691 041 bytes of deliveries, with no line and no field added.
